Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 97, verses 1–5:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} He, the Exalted, says, explaining the virtue of the Qur'an and the loftiness of its status: {Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr)}. [As He, the Exalted, said: {Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night}.] This is because Allah, the Exalted, began sending down the Qur'an in Ramadan, on the Night of Decree, and by it Allah showered the servants with a general mercy for which the servants cannot give adequate thanks. The Night was called "Night of Decree" (laylat al-qadr) because of its great worth and excellence with Allah, and because on it He decrees what will occur during the year concerning lifespans, provisions, and the decreed destinies.

{2} Then He magnified its affair and exalted its worth, saying: {And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?}; that is, its affair is grand and its significance is great.

{3} {The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months}; that is, its excellence equals a thousand months. So the deed performed in it is better than deeds performed in a thousand months devoid of it. This is something that minds are bewildered by and intellects are astonished at, in that [blessed and] exalted Allah bestowed upon this weak nation strength and power through a night in which an act of worship equals and exceeds a thousand months, the lifespan of a man who lived a long life of more than eighty years.

{4} {The angels and the Spirit descend therein}; that is, their descent therein is abundant, {by permission of their Lord for every matter}.

{5} {It is peace until the emergence of dawn}; that is, it is free from every calamity and evil, owing to the abundance of its goodness, {until the emergence of dawn}; that is, its beginning is from sunset and its end is the rising of dawn. The hadiths concerning its virtue are widely transmitted (mutawatir), and that it falls in Ramadan, and in its last ten nights, especially on its odd nights. It remains in every year until the Hour is established. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) would perform i'tikaf and increase his worship in the last ten nights of Ramadan, hoping to attain the Night of Decree. And Allah knows best.
